title: Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships 2027-28: CHF 2,450 a Month and How to Win It
seoDescription: Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships 2027-28: CHF 2,450 monthly, applications open 20 Aug 2026 with country deadlines to late November. Supervisor-first strategy explained.
intro: Switzerland’s Excellence Scholarship pays CHF 2,450 a month for a research stay at ETH, EPFL or any Swiss university — but the supervisor comes first.
description: Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships 2027-28: amounts, country deadlines, supervisor requirement and selection criteria.
author: NextApply Team
excerpt: Swiss Excellence Scholarships 2027-28: CHF 2,450/month and a supervisor-first application strategy.
content:
The Swiss Government Excellence Scholarship is one of Europe’s most generous research awards — and one of the least understood. It is not a degree scholarship in the usual sense: it funds a research stay of six to twelve months at a Swiss university, ETH Zurich, EPFL or one of the ETH-domain institutes, for early-career researchers who already hold a master’s degree. The 2027-28 round opened on 20 August 2026, and because every country’s deadline is different — some close in early October, others run to late November — checking your country’s date is step one.

What it pays

Research scholarships pay CHF 2,450 per month — among the highest government stipends in Europe, sized for Switzerland’s costs, though the official documents stress it is a scholarship, not a salary. Recipients also receive a one-off CHF 300 housing allowance, health insurance, and a half-fare travel card; tuition is typically exempted at public institutions. The standard award runs up to 12 months with a fixed start of 1 September 2027 and no extensions. Art scholarships — open to a smaller list of countries — fund an initial master’s degree in an artistic field, on slightly different terms.

[[chart:swiss-ladder]]

Age matters: the ceiling is 35 (born after a cut-off date stated in the guidelines), and applicants must already hold a master’s or equivalent before departure.

The supervisor comes first

Here is the mechanism that separates winners from rejected files: you must secure a Swiss academic supervisor who agrees to host and mentor your research project before you apply. The application requires their written acceptance. That makes this scholarship less like a lottery and more like a job application — your real task in October is not paperwork but outreach: identifying professors at Swiss institutions whose research matches your project, sending focused emails with your proposal and CV, and converting interest into a signed acceptance.

Selection then runs through Swiss diplomatic representations in your country, with the Federal Commission for Scholarships (FCS) assessing three things: the candidate’s profile, the quality of the research project or artistic work, and synergies for future research cooperation between Switzerland and your country. Final decisions arrive by the end of May 2027 at the latest.

From research stay to full doctorate

Because the award funds months rather than degrees, smart applicants design the stay as a first chapter. A twelve-month stint at ETH, EPFL or Basel does three things at once: it produces a publishable chunk of research, it converts you from cold-contact applicant to internal candidate, and it lets Swiss professors observe your work before committing doctoral funding. Swiss doctoral positions pay real salaries — typically CHF 50,000-90,000 a year depending on canton and institute — so the excellence scholarship is best understood as a funded audition for one of them. Applicants who frame their proposal as the opening move of a longer Swiss research arc give supervisors a reason to say yes twice.

The file itself

The document set is compact but tightly specified: a research project of up to five pages, a CV, two academic references, copies of degrees, and the supervisor’s acceptance letter — plus, for art scholarships, a portfolio. Files are read by academics, so the five-page proposal carries the weight: a sharp question, a method that fits the host group, and a paragraph on cooperation with your home institution. Country quotas make this a national competition, and past laureates from your country are often the best calibration of what wins.

Strategy that matches the mechanics

  • Check your country’s deadline this week. The official SERI list publishes each country’s date — the spread runs from early October to late November 2026, and quotas are national, so you compete only against compatriots.
  • Treat supervisor outreach as the project. Two focused proposals beat ten generic emails; read the group’s recent papers first. Our supervisor email templates transfer directly to Swiss outreach.
  • Write the proposal for cooperation. The third selection criterion rewards projects that build a bridge between your home institution and the Swiss host — say explicitly what continues after the stay ends.
  • Beware phishing. SERI has published an official warning: the application is free, and anyone demanding payment for "visa and social insurance costs" in the scholarship’s name is a scam. No agent can improve your odds.

How it fits a bigger plan

Because the award funds a research stay rather than a full degree, many applicants pair it with a doctoral pathway: the stay becomes a year inside a PhD you fund through a Swiss assistantship afterwards — Swiss doctoral salaries, among the world’s highest, make that arithmetic work, as our country-by-country stipend comparison shows. Others use it as a postdoctoral landing. Either way, the live Swiss listings below — the scholarship card itself plus ETH, EPFL and Lausanne positions — show where the ecosystem you are applying to actually sits.
